system.name: vCXLGen
system.one_liner: a system that automatically synthesizes and formally verifies CXL bridges reconciling different cache-coherence protocols and memory consistency models between hosts

content.subject: how a synthesized MESI-CXL bridge handles a store-miss-from-shared transaction, compared against the original MESI and CXL.mem flows

elements.role: local-protocol (MESI) requester cache issuing the store

elements.name: Br
elements.role: the bridge FSM tracking a compound (LP,GP) state pair for the cache line

elements.name: Gp Dir
elements.role: global-protocol (CXL.mem) directory serving the bridge's memory requests

elements.name: S, S
elements.role: initial bridge state: line Shared in both the local directory and the global cache

elements.name: S, SM
elements.role: transient state after GetM is forwarded, waiting for the global upgrade

elements.name: S, SM^D

elements.name: M, M

relations.what: local store (st) triggers a GetM request
MemRd_A propagates the request into the global CXL.mem domain
Ack grants write permission, completing the local store as a hit

panels.label: (b) Br-MESI-CXL
panels.differs: the paper's synthesized bridge: a compound (LP,GP) FSM forwarding the local GetM into a global MemRd_A/Cmp-E/Data exchange before acking the store

panels.label: (c) MESI
panels.differs: the original local MESI protocol alone: requester sends GetM, the directory invalidates the other sharer (Inv/InvAck) and acks the requester, no bridge involved

panels.label: (d) CXL.mem
panels.differs: the original global CXL.mem protocol alone: the requester's MemRd_A triggers a back-invalidate snoop (BISnpInv/BIRsp-I) on the peer cache before Cmp-E/Data complete the upgrade

content.key_idea: Panel (a)'s pipeline infers translation rules and fuses two protocol FSMs into one bridge FSM; (b) shows the synthesized bridge relaying a store-miss-from-shared request, matching the original MESI (c) and CXL.mem (d) flows it combines.
content.reading_order: Left panel (a) reads top-to-bottom through steps 1-4; the right three panels (b,c,d) are each read top-to-bottom along their lifelines, compared left to right.

summary: Figure 5 documents vCXLGen's two-pass bridge synthesis and validates the result on a store-miss-from-shared example. Panel (a) is a four-step pipeline: step 1 statically analyzes the input GP and LP protocol FSMs to infer translation rules (GP/LP TLTs); steps 2-4 then generate the bridge's compound stable state space, populate its transitions using those rules, and nest the matched remote flow graphs, producing the GP-LP bridge FSM. Panels (b), (c), and (d) compare the same store request as three lane diagrams: (b) shows the synthesized Br-MESI-CXL bridge forwarding a local GetM into a global MemRd_A/Cmp-E/Data exchange before acking the store, while (c) and (d) show the original, unbridged MESI and CXL.mem transaction flows that the synthesis process combined to produce it, so the reader can check the fused behaviour against its two sources message by message.
summary_zh: 图5展示vCXLGen的两遍桥接合成：(a)推断转换规则、生成状态空间、传播并嵌套流，得到GP-LP桥FSM；(b)(c)(d)用泳道图对比合成桥与原始MESI、CXL.mem处理同一store-miss事务的消息序列。
notes: Added 'comparison' as primary group (prior labels had only logic+walkthrough): panels (b),(c),(d) are plainly three side-by-side alternative FSM traces of the same store-miss-from-shared transaction, matching the comparison definition and even the prior pass's own grammar note ('Three side-by-side FSM ladders... trace the same... transaction'); kept logic and walkthrough as secondary since panel (a) is a numbered pipeline and each panel's base is a state machine. Panel (c)'s InvAck routing (sharer to requester vs. sharer to directory) is inferred from typical 3-hop MESI protocols since the low-resolution arrow is ambiguous.
